newsitem.title: GERMANY: German commentators welcome Deutsche Telekom share.
newsitem.headline: German commentators welcome Deutsche Telekom share.

text.p: The sounds of popping champagne corks and clinking glasses appeared to jump from German newspapers on Monday as the press and the financial community celebrated the record listing of Deutsche Telekom AG.

Deutsche Bank, lead manager of the 20 billion mark initial public offering of "T-Shares", placed a full page advertisement in Germany's economic daily Handelsblatt with a picture of an exploding champagne cork branded with a capital "T" and the caption: "From today on it's unstoppable: the T-Share".
The mass daily Bild shouted in bold type above the fold on the title page "Telekom: The Stock Market is Bubbling".

Deutsche Telekom's share offer totals 713 million shares of which 600 million are contained in the basic allotment, another 90 million are part of the so-called Greenshoe, or overallotment, and 23 million shares for employees.
It is Europe's largest-ever shares listing and second in the world only to the enormous offering made by Japan's Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp.

Commentators across the board stressed that Telekom's 100-million-mark advertising campaign appeared to have done what no other share issue in Germany has done before -- it has captured the imagination of millions of ordinary Germans.

It seemed that the question most commentators were asking themselves was whether after the storm of share orders by around two million private individuals the momentum could be maintained and benefit German industry as a whole?

The daily Handelsblatt said: "The price is right. Chances are good that Telekom's share price will climb forcefully in the first days." But the paper also warned hopeful first-time investors: "Shares are and remain risky and can also produce losses."
The daily Sueddeutsche Zeitung pasted a postcard-size picture of Telekom chairman Ron Sommer giving the thumbs-up sign on the title page with the caption: "Turning point to a broader equity culture."
Highlighting this question, the weekly news magazine Der Spiegel put on its cover the picture of a confident Sommer and the title "Testcase Telekom".

Spiegel noted that final judgement was still out on Telekom and its huge listing. "Telekom has already developed into a hit on the stock market, but the former state agency must still become a competitive enterprise."
The daily Die Welt newspaper wrote: "The moment of truth will ring today on the stock exchange."
